# Incident Report — 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | DHCP lease, all suspicious flows sourced here |
| MAC | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | ARP: `18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4` claims `172.17.0.99`; matches DHCP Discover/Request Ethernet source |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP option 12 hostname; confirmed by NBNS name registrations (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`, `<20>`) and mDNS `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.local` |
| Domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (AD domain, DC = WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 / 172.17.0.17) | LDAP `DC=bepositive,DC=com`, Kerberos realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM` |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (Andrew Fletcher) | Kerberos `CNameString=afletcher` in AS/TGS exchanges with the DC; LDAP search result `CN=Andrew Fletcher,CN=Users,DC=bepositive,DC=com` |

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). **Attribution: signature-confirmed.**

The Suricata alert export shows a direct signature hit: `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits, 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80), corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (50 hits, same flow). Following TCP stream 48 in the pcap confirms the exact checkin format the signature keys on: pipe-delimited beacons such as

```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
```

sent via `POST /foots.php` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and a static, spoofed IE7/Trident User-Agent (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; ...)`) — this hardcoded UA on a live Windows 10 host is itself a strong malware indicator, not a real browser.

## Command-and-Control Activity
The infected host beaconed to **79.124.78.197:80** (nginx) roughly every 30–60 seconds from 17:35 UTC for the remainder of the capture (~46 `/foots.php` POSTs observed). A separate gate/registration exchange on the same IP was also captured (TCP stream 51):

- `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` → response: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`
- `POST /index.php` with an encrypted/binary body → single-byte ack `D`

This IP was contacted directly by hardcoded IP address; no DNS lookup for it appears anywhere in the capture.

## Delivery / Staging (behavioral, not content-confirmed)
Immediately before the first Koi Stealer checkin (t=155.4s), the host completed a large encrypted TLS session (701 KB received) to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201:443), starting at t=153.5s. No DNS query for this domain appears in the capture (resolved out-of-band or cached before capture start), and the payload is TLS-encrypted so content cannot be confirmed. Given the timing (ends right as beaconing to the hardcoded C2 IP begins) and the byte volume, this is assessed as the probable payload-delivery/staging connection — flagged as behavioral correlation, not a confirmed download.

## Benign Context (ruled out)
- Standard Windows domain logon sequence at capture start: DHCP, LDAP/CLDAP/Kerberos/DNS to DC 172.17.0.17 (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19).
- `ET INFO Terse Request for .txt`, `ET INFO Microsoft Connection Test` alerts on 23.220.251.149/158 → legitimate `www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt` (NCSI).
- `GPL NETBIOS SMB ...` and `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow` alerts, all between 172.17.0.99 and the DC 172.17.0.17 → generic heuristic signatures known to false-positive on ordinary SMBv1/NTLMSSP negotiation and Kerberos traffic during domain logon; SMB2/DCERPC/SAMR traffic observed is consistent with normal AD logon processing, not exploitation. No second host was contacted, no lateral movement evidence.
- Windows/Office/Bing/MSN telemetry, Windows Update CTL downloads, GoDaddy SSO, and `acroipm2.adobe.com` (legitimate Adobe ARM update-check, response body `****`, benign placeholder).

No cleartext executable transfer was observed via HTTP (all `/foots.php` request bodies are outbound-only octet-stream; `--export-objects http` yielded no PE/executable). Consequently **no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this capture.**
